name: Croatia

findings.summary: Hrvatski Telekom, holding about 45% of Croatian subscribers, named Ericsson Nikola Tesla its sole 5G radio access network supplier until 2024, covering Ericsson Radio System and Spectrum Sharing.
findings.analyst_inference: Equipment vendor Ericsson is Swedish, so pole third (EU); Ericsson Nikola Tesla is its Croatian-listed associate. Hrvatski Telekom is Deutsche Telekom-controlled. Ericsson release tiered S1 as vendor IR on a named contract; no value disclosed. Superseded by the 2024 extension (HRV-002).

findings.summary: Hrvatski Telekom extended Ericsson Nikola Tesla's role as exclusive supplier of its mobile radio access network through end-2027, continuing deployment of Ericsson 5G radio products begun in 2018.
findings.analyst_inference: Single opened S1 (operator press release), so medium. Ericsson is Swedish, so pole third. Value undisclosed. Core vendor separately reported as Ericsson dual-mode 5G Core (search snippet only, not opened, not coded).

findings.summary: A1 Hrvatska signed an exclusive frame agreement with Ericsson Nikola Tesla to upgrade and expand its radio access network with Ericsson Radio System equipment, described as 5G-ready, through end-2023.
findings.analyst_inference: Single opened S1 (vendor company release), so medium. A1 Hrvatska is owned by Austria's A1 Group (America Movil-controlled); pole set by equipment vendor Ericsson (Sweden) = third. Agreement expired end-2023; renewal or successor vendor not found, so still_current null.

findings.summary: Pantheon Atlas announced Pantheon AI, a planned campus of up to 1 GW (800 MW IT) at Topusko, with on-site solar and batteries; construction targeted for early 2027 and full operation by Q1 2029.
findings.analyst_inference: Tier 1: announcement only, no permits, financing or construction reported. Pole us is inferred: Pantheon Atlas is described as a transatlantic group and one of the largest private US investors in Europe, with US DoE envoy support; a Croatian founding partner (Jako Andabak) is named, so control could be mixed. Headline EUR 50bn includes tenants' IT spend (campus EUR 12bn); USD conversions in sources differ (54bn vs 58bn), so announced_value_usd left null. Design cites Nvidia GW-scale AI factory standards; no chips ordered.

findings.local_actor: University of Zagreb University Computing Centre (SRCE)
findings.summary: SRCE launched Supek, Croatia's most powerful supercomputer, an HPE Cray system of about 1.25 PFLOPS with roughly 80 Nvidia A100 GPUs; SRCE's separate Vrancic cloud adds 16 A100s.
findings.analyst_inference: Equipment vendors HPE and Nvidia are US, so pole us. SRCE page states 80 GPUs in its table and 81 in text. still_current true because SRCE's current documentation lists Supek as in service. Modest scale; funding source not stated (minister cited EU recovery and cohesion research programmes).
